title: Spring
summary: On a mild spring morning, Carrie, Bjorn and Gunnar wait for a bus while the Vikings quietly inventory the season ahead rather than merely enjoying the weather.
settingText: Bushwick bus stop, mild spring morning
panelPlan: Wide: Ordinary Bushwick bus stop in clear mild spring weather. Street trees are budding, people wear light jackets, and fresh green growth appears in sidewalk planters. Carrie checks the street for the bus while Bjorn and Gunnar watch the neighborhood.
Medium: Gunnar studies new leaves on a street tree and the soft ground around its roots.
Two-shot: Bjorn asks Gunnar a practical household question as if continuing an earlier conversation.
Medium: Carrie hears the answer and looks over.
Close: Gunnar counts briefly on his fingers, thinking in seasons rather than weeks.

dialogueInline.text: How much have we put by?

source: Issue 8 — Provision. Spring provisioning / public-land / weather material developed and locked in September 2026.

title: It Is April
summary: Carrie initially thinks winter planning in spring is excessive; Bjorn and Gunnar treat spring as the obvious beginning of winter provision.
settingText: Bushwick bus stop, spring morning
panelPlan: Three-shot: Carrie looks from the budding trees to Bjorn and Gunnar, genuinely checking that she heard correctly.
Medium: Bjorn answers without defensiveness.
Close on Carrie: She gestures at the warm morning around them.
Two-shot on the Vikings: Gunnar and Bjorn exchange a brief look because her objection does not make sense to them.
Wide: The bus has not arrived; ordinary pedestrians move through the spring morning.

dialogueInline.text: That is why we are asking.

source: Issue 8 — Provision. Spring provisioning / public-land / weather material developed and locked in September 2026.

title: Before the Leaves Burn
summary: The Vikings explain that winter food begins with spring work; waiting until autumn means the growing season has already been spent.
settingText: Bushwick bus stop, spring morning
panelPlan: Medium: Gunnar crouches briefly to touch damp soil at the edge of a tree bed, checking it by habit rather than proposing to plant there.
Two-shot: Bjorn names planting, growing, gathering and preserving as one continuous seasonal process.
Close on Gunnar: He looks up through the new spring leaves.
Medium on Carrie: The logic lands; she stops treating the timing as the strange part.
Wide: A city bus turns into view in the distance.

dialogueInline.text: If we are to grow food, we cannot begin when the leaves are already aflame with color.
By then the growing is finished.

source: Issue 8 — Provision. Spring provisioning / public-land / weather material developed and locked in September 2026.

title: What Have We Stored
summary: A quick inventory reveals that the household has ordinary groceries and some durable food, but nothing resembling a winter store.
settingText: Bushwick bus stop as the bus approaches
panelPlan: Medium: Bjorn asks Gunnar for the household inventory while Carrie listens.
Close: Gunnar mentally counts the durable food currently in 5B.
Medium: Carrie starts to understand that they mean months of provision, not emergency groceries.
Wide: The bus pulls to the curb and opens its doors.
Three-shot: They step toward the bus while the conversation continues.

dialogueInline.text: Bread for two days. Dried meat. Some rice. Apples.
What did you think we meant?

source: Issue 8 — Provision. Spring provisioning / public-land / weather material developed and locked in September 2026.

title: Food Keeps Coming
summary: On the bus, Carrie explains the modern premise that households do not usually store a winter's food because commercial supply continues through the season.
settingText: NYC city bus, moving through Brooklyn in spring
panelPlan: Wide interior: Carrie, Bjorn and Gunnar sit or stand together on an ordinary city bus. Spring streets move past the windows.
Two-shot: Carrie explains the basic premise plainly rather than listing every piece of infrastructure at once.
Close on Bjorn: He checks that she literally means food remains available in winter.
Medium: Gunnar looks through the bus window as a grocery delivery truck passes in the opposite direction.
Three-shot: Carrie confirms that stores are replenished continuously.

dialogueInline.text: You don't usually store a whole winter here.
No one place. That's the point.

source: Issue 8 — Provision. Spring provisioning / public-land / weather material developed and locked in September 2026.

title: From Where
summary: The supply chain impresses the Vikings as a large coordinated achievement, but its length immediately becomes visible to them.
settingText: NYC city bus, moving through Brooklyn
panelPlan: Medium: Gunnar turns from the window with the obvious next question.

Sequence panel: Carrie names farms in other regions, warmer climates, warehouses, refrigerated storage, trucks, rail and ships while the city moves past outside; do not render invented explanatory labels.
Close on Bjorn: He is impressed rather than dismissive.
Close on Gunnar: He follows the causal chain farther than Carrie initially intended.
Wide: The bus passes delivery traffic and ordinary storefront loading activity.

dialogueInline.text: Fair. Farms upstate. Other states. Warmer places. Warehouses. Trucks. Ships.
Growers, distributors, stores. Orders. Prices. Demand.
And none of them know us.

source: Issue 8 — Provision. Spring provisioning / public-land / weather material developed and locked in September 2026.

title: A Strong System
summary: Bjorn recognizes the supply network as powerful while Gunnar notes its dependence on many unseen links; their response is supplementation, not rejection.
settingText: City bus arriving near Maria Hernandez Park, spring
panelPlan: Two-shot: Bjorn considers the scale of the system with sincere respect.
Medium: Gunnar lists only the vulnerabilities that follow directly from the chain Carrie described: road, storage, fuel and timing.
Close on Carrie: She explains that the system has alternatives and inventory precisely because individual links sometimes fail.
Wide through bus window: Green park space comes into view as the bus approaches their stop.
Three-shot: They rise to exit; Bjorn looks toward the open ground outside.

dialogueInline.text: Other warehouses. Stored stock. Emergency generators sometimes.
So the system expects parts to fail.
Yes. That's part of making it strong.

source: Issue 8 — Provision. Spring provisioning / public-land / weather material developed and locked in September 2026.

title: Good Ground
summary: In the park, Bjorn and Gunnar evaluate spring ground the same way they evaluated the apartment and city systems: for practical use.
settingText: Maria Hernandez Park, spring daytime
panelPlan: Wide: Maria Hernandez Park in ordinary spring use: walkers, families, benches, budding trees and open green areas. Carrie, Bjorn and Gunnar cross the park after leaving the bus.
Medium: Gunnar slows near a sunny open strip and presses the soil lightly with the toe of his boot.
Medium: Bjorn looks at sun exposure, slope and foot traffic rather than treating the park as scenery.
Two-shot: Gunnar points out that the ground is already soft enough to work.
Close on Carrie: She has not yet realized where the conversation is going.
source: Issue 8 — Provision. Spring provisioning / public-land / weather material developed and locked in September 2026.

title: A Small Field
summary: The Vikings make a modest, competent plan to supplement rather than replace the city's food supply.
settingText: Maria Hernandez Park, spring daytime
panelPlan: Wide: Bjorn and Gunnar stand at the edge of the open area, visually dividing the available ground by light and use without stepping into occupied recreation space.
Medium: Gunnar indicates one sunnier strip for hardy food crops and a smaller edge for roots or greens; keep crop depiction generic and seasonally plausible.
Close on Bjorn: He deliberately scales the plan down rather than claiming the whole park.
Medium on Carrie: Realization arrives.
Three-shot: Carrie stops walking.

dialogueInline.text: Roots along there. Greens where the shade starts.

source: Issue 8 — Provision. Spring provisioning / public-land / weather material developed and locked in September 2026.

title: You Cannot Plant the Park
summary: Carrie stops the plan before anyone touches the ground, and the Vikings are confused by the prohibition rather than by the concept of public land.
settingText: Maria Hernandez Park, spring daytime
panelPlan: Three-shot: Carrie makes clear that she is stopping the proposed planting, not accusing them of having already done anything.
Medium: Bjorn looks down at the unused spring ground, then back at Carrie.
Two-shot: Gunnar asks the practical ownership question.
Medium: Carrie answers plainly.
Wide: Other park users continue normal recreation around them.

dialogueInline.text: I'm getting ahead of the shovel.
Then we are asking the wrong person.
No. I am saving you time.
The city owns it for everyone.
Everyone can use it as a park.

source: Issue 8 — Provision. Spring provisioning / public-land / weather material developed and locked in September 2026.

title: Then Ask the City
summary: Bjorn's obvious solution is permission; Carrie's certainty that this particular park will not become their field exposes a different relationship to shared land.
settingText: Maria Hernandez Park, spring daytime
panelPlan: Two-shot: Bjorn treats city ownership as a person-or-authority problem that should be solvable by asking.
Medium: Carrie explains that this park has a designated public use and cannot simply be converted to private food production.
Close on Gunnar: He distinguishes permission from the merits of their plan.
Medium on Carrie: She confirms that the answer does not depend on whether their planting plan is competent.
Wide: Bjorn studies the open ground again.

dialogueInline.text: Without hearing what we would plant?
That is a name, not a reason.
The reason is people already agreed what this land is for.
And empty ground remains empty because of the agreement.
Sometimes shared space only stays shared because nobody gets to claim the useful-looking part.

source: Issue 8 — Provision. Spring provisioning / public-land / weather material developed and locked in September 2026.

title: There Are Gardens
summary: Carrie gives them the real modern alternative: community gardens exist, but access is organized and limited rather than simply claimed.
settingText: Maria Hernandez Park bench, spring daytime
panelPlan: Medium: The three sit or pause near a park bench as Carrie shifts from prohibition to an actual alternative.
Two-shot: She explains that community gardens and garden groups do exist in the city.
Close on Gunnar: He immediately asks how to get ground there.
Medium: Carrie gives the basic answer: find a garden, ask whether it has room, join its rules.
Close on Bjorn: He accepts that this is at least a path.

dialogueInline.text: Depends. City land, nonprofits, garden groups.
Find one with room. Ask. Join. Follow their rules.
Could be quick. Could be a waiting list.
That is better than no path.

source: Issue 8 — Provision. Spring provisioning / public-land / weather material developed and locked in September 2026.

title: Not This Spring
summary: The possibility of a garden does not solve the immediate seasonal problem; Bjorn notices that permission and access operate on a slower timetable than planting.
settingText: Maria Hernandez Park, spring daytime
panelPlan: Wide: New leaves and active spring park life emphasize that the growing season is already underway.
Two-shot: Bjorn asks whether Carrie can guarantee them usable garden ground in time to plant.
Close on Carrie: She cannot.
Medium: Gunnar looks again at the ground they could physically work today but are not permitted to use.
Three-shot: Carrie does not try to pretend the delay is irrelevant.

dialogueInline.text: Can we plant there this week?
Then it may not solve this spring.
Permission comes after the season begins.
Then the rule wastes a season.
It also stops fifty people from each claiming the same patch.
Spring does not wait for permission.

source: Issue 8 — Provision. Spring provisioning / public-land / weather material developed and locked in September 2026.

title: Money I Do Not Earn
summary: The provisioning discussion reaches Bjorn's real problem: the city's food system can feed the household, but his role in making that provision possible is unclear.
settingText: Maria Hernandez Park edge, spring afternoon
panelPlan: Medium: Bjorn looks from the park to an ordinary grocery bag carried by a passerby.
Two-shot: He reduces the modern food system to its practical chain: other people grow it, move it and sell it.
Close on Carrie: She hears the shift from agricultural planning to Bjorn's provider identity.
Close on Bjorn: He names the missing piece without anger.
Wide: Gunnar stands beside them, serious; nobody has a quick answer.

dialogueInline.text: With money I do not earn.

source: Issue 8 — Provision. Spring provisioning / public-land / weather material developed and locked in September 2026.

title: The Wind Changed
summary: Later the same spring day, Gunnar reads an approaching storm from immediate physical signs before Carrie's phone forecast suggests it will arrive.
settingText: Bushwick fire escape and apartment window, late afternoon
panelPlan: Wide: Late-afternoon spring light over Bushwick. Clouds have thickened in the distance, but the block below is still active.
Medium on fire escape: Gunnar stops mid-conversation and feels the wind shift across his face and clothing.
Close: He looks at the lower cloud line and the moving tree canopy below.
Interior/threshold two-shot: Bjorn sees Gunnar's attention change and asks one question.
Medium: Carrie checks her phone forecast from inside the window.

dialogueInline.text: My phone says rain around six.

source: Issue 8 — Provision. Spring provisioning / public-land / weather material developed and locked in September 2026.

title: Before the Rain
summary: The household prepares efficiently for an ordinary spring storm: not panic, just securing the things weather can damage.
settingText: Bushwick apartment, fire escape and roof access, late afternoon
panelPlan: Wide: Bjorn assigns no formal commands; the household simply moves. Astrid brings loose fabric and small items in from the fire escape while the two male Kin close and latch windows.
Medium: Gunnar checks the roof access and confirms the contained rooftop stove/fire pit is cold, covered and secure; no fire is burning.
Medium: Bjorn moves books, paper records and the household ledger away from the window area.
Close on Carrie: She watches the practiced preparation and realizes nobody is behaving as if this is an emergency.
Three-shot: Carrie asks whether they expect something severe.
source: Issue 8 — Provision. Spring provisioning / public-land / weather material developed and locked in September 2026.

directionInline.text: The rooftop stove/fire pit is cold and fully extinguished before the storm. Show competent weather preparation, not survivalist panic.

title: Later
summary: The upstairs neighbor checks a phone forecast and expects the storm later; Astrid trusts the immediate weather signs without making the neighbor foolish.
settingText: Fifth-floor hallway and apartment doorway, late afternoon
panelPlan: Medium: Astrid steps into the hallway to bring in or check one last small item near the apartment door.
Two-shot: The Upstairs Neighbor emerges carrying an umbrella but otherwise unhurried.
Close: The neighbor glances at a phone forecast.
Medium: Astrid looks toward the hallway window where tree branches have begun moving harder.
Wide: Gunnar passes behind Astrid carrying nothing dramatic, just a towel and a small bucket for the window area.
source: Issue 8 — Provision. Spring provisioning / public-land / weather material developed and locked in September 2026.

title: Now They Know
summary: Carrie's weather alert arrives only after the household has already completed most of its preparation.
settingText: Bushwick studio apartment, late afternoon
panelPlan: Wide: The apartment is now orderly for the storm: windows latched, loose exterior items inside, papers away from glass, towels accessible.
Insert: Carrie's phone gives an audible weather-alert chime; no readable alert text is required on screen.
Medium: Carrie checks the phone and looks toward Gunnar.
Close on Gunnar: He does not celebrate being right.
Wide: The room goes briefly darker as the cloud line reaches the block.
source: Issue 8 — Provision. Spring provisioning / public-land / weather material developed and locked in September 2026.

title: First Gust
summary: The storm arrives sooner than the casual forecast implied, but because the household prepared, the first hard gust creates inconvenience rather than crisis.
settingText: Bushwick studio apartment and fire escape during spring thunderstorm
panelPlan: Exterior wide: A hard spring gust drives rain across the block; tree branches bend and pedestrians hurry under awnings.
Interior medium: The window shudders once against its latch while the room remains dry.
Medium: Bjorn checks the roof/fire-escape access visually without opening it into the wind.
Close on Carrie: Thunder lands close enough to make her look up from the phone.
Wide: Everyone remains where they already chose to be; no scrambling is required.
source: Issue 8 — Provision. Spring provisioning / public-land / weather material developed and locked in September 2026.

title: Nothing Happened
summary: Preparation makes the storm narratively uneventful, which lets Carrie understand what Viking competence often looks like when it works.
settingText: Bushwick studio apartment during storm
panelPlan: Wide: Heavy rain continues outside while the household resumes ordinary indoor activity under safe conditions.
Medium: Astrid folds the fabric brought in from outside; First Male Kin checks one towel by the window; Second Male Kin returns to his prior task.
Medium: Carrie looks around, almost expecting another action.
Two-shot: Bjorn sits down now that the preparation is finished.
Close: Carrie realizes the absence of a crisis is the result.
source: Issue 8 — Provision. Spring provisioning / public-land / weather material developed and locked in September 2026.

title: Tomorrow
summary: After the storm, Carrie acknowledges the household's weather competence and offers to investigate community gardens; Bjorn immediately adds the unresolved provision problem that will drive Trial of Toil: work.
settingText: Bushwick fire escape and studio apartment after the spring storm
panelPlan: Wide exterior: The storm has passed. Wet roofs and streets reflect clearing evening light; water drips from the fire escape and new spring leaves.
Medium at the open window/fire-escape threshold: Carrie, Bjorn and Gunnar look out at the clearing sky while the Kin resume ordinary household tasks behind them.
Two-shot: Carrie acknowledges that Gunnar read the storm correctly and Bjorn's preparation worked.
Medium: Carrie brings the earlier park conversation back into the practical world by offering to ask about community gardens.
Close on Bjorn: He accepts that, then names the problem the garden cannot solve.
Final wide: The household is safe, dry and provisioned for tonight; the wet city continues outside.

dialogueInline.text: You were right about the storm.

source: Issue 8 — Provision. Spring provisioning / public-land / weather material developed and locked in September 2026.
